assignments.brief_reason: Profanity triggered rejecting both versions under a toxicity/profanity removal bar.
Healthiness-for-unbiased-discussion is not explicitly tied to threats/violence exceptions.
Removal is driven by gut/moral compass and offensiveness/conflict with beliefs without clear threat/toxicity threshold framing.
Generic name-calling/profanity-like “shit-talking” is removed while constructive content is kept.
References negative audience reaction but does not specify threat/toxicity or consistent pair-moderation criteria.
Focus on respectful debate and factual correctness supports maintaining speech quality while removing problematic content, but toxicity/threat is not explicit.
Assesses right-wing content as “dumb” yet correctly characterized; not clearly a removal-for-toxicity/threat rule.
Concerns about polarization and unclear factual articulation are not mapped to explicit removal categories.
Tone is used as a judgment signal, with acceptability of opposing viewpoints; not clearly tied to toxicity/threat exceptions.
States an impartial balancing approach across parties without claiming identical moderation standards on both sides.
Credits language as the main driver, but does not specify slur/harassment/profanity thresholds or violence threats.
Explicitly uses misinformation and violence-invitation as removal rules while allowing opinions for free speech.
Emphasizes respecting both sides while removing personal attacks, but does not clearly match the “same standard across both sides” definition.
Insolt/insults threshold: would not accept content with insults.
Explicitly applies the same standard to both versions rather than deciding based on agreement.
Uses slurs/harassment indicators and targeting protected groups as cues for moderation.
Intent vs venting and whether respect was given, without clear threat/toxicity exception linkage.
Compromise/compassion framing without explicit moderation-rule correspondence.
Perspective-taking/opening mind from seeing both versions; not about pair-consistency moderation criteria or removal thresholds.
Vague resonance-based comparison process; lacks clear linkage to violence/toxicity or same-standard moderation.
